problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=-3xy.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/c35c98904d2a0d0d6d49c582cd9f9dba9d96e91ae0da5deb2d329f38f77532e3.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/9340582eaad37c4ce1e0c8cbcdce48faec1e36c3c05adbedd61aa2de7168fd2f.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-3x$ | $y$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\ge 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/3cfdf7d548c430f225a78fa6c4d915d69207f0a1c090d13cdd530c90865731ef.png)
